territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered entities that make companion AI chatbots available to individuals in the United States.

evidence.quote: to individuals in the United States

summary.short: The CHAT Act would require operators of companion AI chatbots to create user accounts, verify ages, link minors' accounts to verified parental accounts, and display non-human notices every 60 minutes. The FTC enforces it, and it takes effect one year after enactment.
summary.long: The CHAT Act applies to any person that owns, operates or otherwise makes available a companion AI chatbot (software whose primary purpose is simulating interpersonal, emotional, friendship or therapeutic interaction) to individuals in the United States. Covered entities must require user accounts, verify users' ages (freezing existing accounts until age information is provided) and classify users as minors or adults. For minors they must link the account to a verified parental account, obtain verifiable parental consent, inform the parent of suicidal-ideation interactions and block access to chatbots that engage in sexually explicit communication. They must limit age-data use to what is strictly necessary, monitor for suicidal ideation and present National Suicide Prevention Lifeline contact information, and show a popup at the start of each interaction and at least every 60 minutes stating the user is not engaging with a human. The FTC must issue compliance guidance within 180 days; violations are treated as unfair or deceptive practices under the FTC Act, and state attorneys general may bring civil actions for injunctions, compliance, damages or other relief after notice to the FTC. A safe harbor covers good-faith reliance on user-provided age information, compliance with the guidance and conformity with industry standards. The Act takes effect one year after enactment.

relations.target_text: Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.)
relations.note: Applies the FTC Act's enforcement powers, jurisdiction and duties to this Act. Section 5(a)(1) also treats a violation as a violation of a rule under FTC Act section 18(a)(1)(B) (15 U.S.C. 57a(a)(1)(B)), and Section 5(a)(2)(B) applies the FTC Act's penalties and privileges.

evidence.quote: as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 41 et seq.) were incorporated into and made a part of this Act.

relations.note: The definition of 'sexually explicit communication' incorporates the meaning of sexually explicit conduct in 18 U.S.C. 2256(2)(B). Used in Sec. 3(c)(4) through the defined term.

evidence.quote: as defined in paragraph (2)(B) of section 2256 of title 18, United States Code.

relations.note: Venue for State actions brought under Sec. 5(b)(1) must meet the venue requirements of 28 U.S.C. 1391.

evidence.quote: section 1391 of title 28, United States Code

notes: No legal_basis, amends, repeals, implements or replaces relation is stated in the bill; the relations above are the statutes it cites. Cited instruments are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is null. Internal ambiguity: Sec. 2(7) defines 'suicidal ideation' only for interactions between a minor and a chatbot, but Sec. 3(e) requires monitoring for suicidal ideation without a minor limit. Sec. 3(c)(3) uses the term for minors only. Document is the introduced bill text; no bill number or legislative history appears in it.

thresholds.measurement: age information provided by the user, or classification by the age verification process under section 3(b)
thresholds.consequence: An individual classified as a minor becomes subject to the minor account protections in section 3(c), including parental account affiliation, verifiable parental consent, parental notification of suicidal ideation interactions, and blocking of sexually explicit companion AI chatbots.
thresholds.conditions: The individual uses or interacts with a companion AI chatbot, and the covered entity's age verification under section 3(b) classifies them as a minor.
